summary: Kogi Kudara (1945–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He taught Yutaka Kanazawa, was a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1979, 1997), and served as editor for the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).

Koichi Hokazono (b. 1944) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned his PhD at Kyushu University, holding posts at Kyushu University (attested 1995) and The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991–2000).

Koichi Shinohara (b. 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004), Numata Program coordinator at the University of Toronto Mississauga (attested 2004), and senior lecturer at Yale University (~2004–2017).

Koichi Takahashi (b. 1973) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Tokyo in 2004 under Akira Saito and Yasunori Ejima, and held research and assistant posts there in 2005 and 2015.

Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an MA at the University of Tokyo, studying under Akira Hirakawa and Gyōin Hashimoto, and served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1975–2006).
Koin Takada (1924–1998) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Ryukoku University (~1944–1947). A disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto, he succeeded him in 1967.

Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) studied Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at Kyoto University (~1957–1963) under Yutaka Ochihara, he lectured at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and was an assistant professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University, where he served as assistant professor (~1969–2004) and professor (~1976–2004), and was an editor for Bukkyō Bunka Kenkyū.

Kojiro Yoshikawa (1904–1980) was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and board chairman of Toho Gakkai (~1972–1980).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate at Waseda University studying under Sokichi Tsuda, served as professor at Waseda (1941–1969), and served as president of Taisho University (1928–1968, 1972–1975).
Kojun Saito (1930–2002) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Seiren Matsunami and was a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita (b. 1944) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under Yujun Endo and held a professorship at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki (1931–2008) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Rissho University (~1950–1960), he served there as assistant professor (~1968–1975), department head (~1975–2002), and director/professor (~1992–2002), teaching Guohui Shi.
Koki Kawagishi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and International Buddhist University (attested 1976).
Konchok Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Dilgo Khyentse.
Konchok Gyatso works in Tibetology. He studied under Sherab Gyatso and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Konchok Zangpo studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Konrad Klaus (b. 1956) is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Göttingen and Marburg under Michael Hahn. He held visiting professorships at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn (1999–2001), succeeding Claus Vogel in 2001.

Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905), he held posts there (~1906–1909) and at Kyoto University (~1909–1938), teaching Seiichi Mizuno.

Kosei Ishii (b. 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a doctorate at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa, and later held posts at Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006) and Komazawa University as professor (2006–2021).
